# Step 2.228: the role-against-command test, whole

## Builder 1: allowed or refused, for the missing people and league states

What exists, all in `packages/database/src/stores/role-matrix.test.ts` (no command changed, no migration):

- 19 kinds of person against every row (was 12): added a registrar, editor and scorekeeper limited to one program, a coach and a captain. The coach's and captain's grant is moved onto the team the call is about (its `teamId`, the team of its `rosterEntryId`, or the home team of its `gameId`), so "their own team" is tried; they hold nothing a stage 2 command needs (P4 §4, T-500).
- Club admin: the database still refuses a club scope (0008); a test proves it, so it fails the day clubs can be given. The header now says this, and is true.
- Every row again in an archived and in a suspended league, as each person allowed in a working league: reads work, every change is refused except U-9's and R-26's (cancel an invitation, remove access, take a scorekeeper off a game, a name request for less, un-archive), written by hand (T-501, T-502). A separate test moves "Names on public pages" toward less (works) and back toward more (refused) in an archived league.
- Every `games.score` row in a league that scores assigned games only: the owner, a scheduler and the assigned scorekeeper succeed; a second scorekeeper without the assignment is refused on a call about one game.
- Broken by hand and seen to fail, then restored: a scorekeeper scoring a game not assigned to them, a coach allowed a roster command, a roster change succeeding in an archived league.
- Pending decisions T-500, T-501, T-502; T4 §12's row now names roles and league states.

Run and passed: the matrix (856 passed, 2 todo, 225 s, was 67 s), the other stores tests (30 files, 254), `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`.

Findings for the lead (not changed in code):

- `leagues.remove_draft`: our staff removed a never-published league that was archived or suspended; the command refuses only a published or used league. U-9 says read-only; the spec does not say whether staff may still remove such a draft. Marked `todo` with `FINDING:` in `stateFindings`.
- T-501 is a reading the spec does not spell out: reads that open a change (score sheet, tracker state and rosters, a game's format, reopen and put-back offers, the tracked box score grid, the season rules preview, the adjustments list) are refused in a read-only league, as the code does. If the lead reads U-9 otherwise, those are product faults.
- Refusal codes differ by command in a read-only league: "not-allowed", "league-read-only" (invitations), "illegal-transition" (publishing a suspended league), "invitation-not-usable" (reading a link).

For builder 2 (T-76, the fields each read gives): `runRow(row, actor, before, accountOf)` returns only the outcome code; widen it to hand back the result's value, write by hand per read command the fields each kind of person may see (P4 §4, T-76: a scorekeeper's roster read never has a date of birth), and add the done test's fourth case: break one read to give a field and see the matrix fail. The `readCommands` and `changeToolReads` sets list the reads.

## Builder 2: what each read gives each person (T-76), and S-132

What exists:

- Every read (the 37 commands of `readCommands`, `changeToolReads` and reading an invitation link) is checked in the main sweep, for every person allowed, field by field: `runRowFor` hands back the result, `fieldsOf` turns it into paths, and `packages/database/src/stores/role-matrix-fields.test-helper.ts` lists, by hand, what each read gives: `all`, a `guarded` field given only to a holder of its permission (R-16: a person's birth date, contact email and under-18 flag behind `people.read_sensitive`), and `byActor` (S-38's reopen offers; one's own grants in `my_access`). A test proves every read has a list and every list a read (T-503).
- Each read runs with a person who has every private field R-16 names, on the roster of the team the call is about (and the person a call reads is made the same), so a list that would be empty cannot hide a leak. T-76's own case holds: the tracker's rosters and the score sheet give a scorekeeper names and jerseys, no birth date.
- S-132 (Decided for you): our staff may remove a never-published league that is archived or suspended; the `todo` is now a row expecting it; P2 (U-9) says so.
- Broken by hand and seen to fail, then restored: the game roster query (`queries/list-game-roster.ts`) handing out `players[].birthDate`; both tracker-roster rows failed on the fields check.

Run and passed: the matrix (859 passed, 0 todo, 289 s, was 225 s: the private person made for every read run, and the two remove-draft rows), the other stores tests (30 files, 254), `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`.

For the lead (list B, not built): in a read-only league the refusal code differs by command ("not-allowed", "league-read-only", "illegal-transition", "invitation-not-usable").

What I distrust: the `all` lists are what each read gives today, checked against R-16 and T-76 for private fields, not derived field by field from a spec that does not list every field; some reads still return empty lists in their fixtures (divisions, venues, activity), so their item fields are not pinned. No role holds `people.read` without `people.read_sensitive` today, so the guarded split is proved only by the break above, not by a second kind of reader. The matrix is now near 300 s.

- H2: `withOneOfEach` gives every read one of each thing it lists (games of both programs, invitations, an activity entry, binned rows, a division, a venue and court, an adjustment, a coin flip, level teams, a box score line); the fields helper now holds the items' fields. `filledLists` pins the reviewed reads to give the owner no empty list. - M1: the five games lists check which games (by label) each person is given: the program-limited only the other program's, and in "assigned games only" the scorekeeper only their assigned ones, the unassigned one none. Break: `my-games-of.ts` letting everyone see every game failed four rows; restored.
- M2: `settingNeeds` writes each setting's permission by hand; a test compares it with core's.
- M3 and L1 left to the lead.

Run and passed: the matrix (860 passed, 293 s, was 289 s), the other stores tests, `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, the pending decisions test.
